sections.name: How to read it
summary: Which TCE each route shows, and what every figure leaves out.

method: Every route is priced on its latest dated rate, the preset the calculator opens for it, by the same engine and conventions as the rest of the study: the Baltic's round voyage, its ships, speeds and port days, bunkers at the hub with public prices nearest the loading port, and a 5 percent weather margin on steaming time.

Tanker rates are quoted in Worldscale points, and a point has no dollar value without the licensed flat rate, so for the tanker routes the TCE shown is the Baltic's own, printed beside the rate in its weekly report. Where the rate is a lump sum (TD22, TC20) the engine prices the same voyage, and both figures are shown. The Baltic publishes no TCE for the dry voyage routes: theirs is the engine's estimate at a public rate. S4A is a trip time charter, so its TCE is the owner's over the round trip, the ballast back to the US Gulf included.

Port charges have no public per call figure and are left out of every TCE, as each panel says; so are canal tolls where a routing uses a canal. An alternative that earns more only because it leaves out a toll or a premium says so.

The lines are the ones the distances are measured on. The map is equirectangular and not to scale, so it carries no distance bar. TC23, the intra-EEA Handy route, is priced only for its carbon cost, on the Carbon view.
